# Cache placement, freshness and replicas

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `architecture-cache-replicas` · **Architecture & Distributed Systems** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S01-Q044](#S01-Q044)

<p>How would you choose between in-memory and distributed caching for a service? Explain the constraint that would make you switch approaches.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Choose a caching design that meets the read contract across the stated number of replicas.</p>

<ul>
<li>Define the authoritative source and tolerated staleness.</li>
<li>Compare in-process and distributed placement with a read/update trace.</li>
<li>Plan invalidation, cache-failure behavior and replica checks.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>A cache choice starts with which data may be reused and for how long. Placement then changes who can see an update, so replica behavior follows directly from the freshness contract.</p>

<a id="S01-Q043"></a>

### S01-Q043 · Foundation

<p>What caching approaches would you consider for a .NET application? Explain the decision factors before choosing a particular technology.</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q043](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q043)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q043](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q043)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What caching approaches are available in .NET applications?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Identify what is cached, who owns the authoritative data and how readers tolerate older values. A catalog of cache products is not a caching strategy.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Frame a caching decision from data and workload requirements.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a hypothetical read path with an explicit freshness requirement; product-specific APIs or defaults require separate official verification.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects placement, lifetime and invalidation to the data contract.</li>
<li>Explains a case where caching adds risk or provides too little benefit and proposes validation.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Adding a cache without specifying freshness, invalidation or the source of truth.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you decide whether this read path needs a cache at all?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S01-Q044"></a>

### S01-Q044 · Trade-offs

<p>How would you choose between in-memory and distributed caching for a service? Explain the constraint that would make you switch approaches.</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q044](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q044)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q044](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q044)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare in-memory cache and distributed cache.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare where cached state lives and how readers reach it. Include consistency, dependency failures and operational cost rather than using speed as the only criterion.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Defend cache placement under a stated service contract.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State replica count, tolerated staleness and the authoritative data source; do not assume a distributed cache provides every desired consistency guarantee.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces a read and an update across the proposed cache boundary.</li>
<li>Explains the principal failure mode and a condition that favors the alternative.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming local caching is always faster overall or distributed caching is automatically consistent.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should the service do if the selected cache is unavailable?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S01-Q045"></a>

### S01-Q045 · Production decision

<p>What changes in a caching design when a .NET service moves from one instance to multiple replicas? Trace an update and later reads on different instances.</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q045](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q045)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q045](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q045)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What changes when the application runs on multiple replicas?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Keep the source’s caching context: reason about ownership, separate state and stale reads across replicas. Do not turn this into an unrelated catalogue of scaling technologies.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reassess shared-state assumptions across deployment replicas.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a hypothetical multi-instance service, a stated freshness contract and rolling deployment; any provider-specific guarantees need official verification.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces what different readers can observe and identifies invalidation or refresh boundaries.</li>
<li>Plans checks for replica divergence, cache failure and deployment transitions.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming adding replicas leaves every in-process state assumption unchanged.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you detect inconsistent cached values without inspecting each instance manually?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A hypothetical service caches a frequently read product summary and grows from one instance to three. Specify permitted staleness, trace an update followed by reads on different replicas, and compare two placements. Describe the user-visible result during cache unavailability and checks for divergence.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Describes both placements and states a freshness requirement.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Explains update visibility, failure handling and the constraint that would change the choice.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Product names or a claimed latency reduction alone do not establish consistency or the benefit of caching.</p>
